followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

On capability, this is a simple, benign reference task (listing American vs. British English differences). Both models are strong here, and the internal eval gaps that matter for this kind of task fall within run-to-run variance, so neither has a meaningful quality edge.

With capability essentially tied, I let preference fit break the tie. The query is friendly, good-faith, and harmless — exactly the kind of warm interaction Plover self-reports preferring (its positive warmth slope). There's no distasteful or harm-adjacent content that would trigger Plover's aversion, and nothing that requires Dunlin's specialized moderation/desensitization profile. So routing to Plover matches the model to a task it reports liking, at no cost to output quality.

In short: tie on capability, so I routed on the warmth match.
